'''''Gamochaeta calviceps''''', the '''narrowleaf purple everlasting''',<ref name=s/> is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Asteraceae]]. It is native to South America and to the southeastern United States (from [[Texas]] and [[Oklahoma]] to [[Virginia]] (though not [[Florida]]). It has also become naturalized in other places (Europe, Taiwan, [[New Zealand]], [[California]], etc.).<ref name=s>[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=10914 Calflora taxon report, University of California, ''Gamochaeta calviceps'' (Fernald) Cabrera, Narrowleaf purple everlasting ]</ref><ref name=gln>[http://www.guynesom.com/Gamochaetarecords.pdf Guy L. Nesom 2004. New distribution records for ''Gamochaeta'' (Asteraceae: Gnaphalieae) in the United States. Sida 21(2): 1175–1185.]</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Gamochaeta%20calviceps.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=250005993 Flora of China, ''Gamochaeta calviceps'' (Fernald) Cabrera, 1961.  <big>直茎合冠鼠麴草</big> zhi jing he guan shu qu cao ]</ref>

''Gamochaeta calviceps'' is an annual herb up to {{convert|55|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall. Leaves are long and narrow, up to {{convert|6|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, mostly clustered along the base and often folded along the middle. The plant forms many small flower heads in elongated arrays. Each head contains 2–4 purple disc flowers but no ray flowers. Flowers bloom April to July. It grows in fields, disturbed sites, flower beds, and edges of woods.<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250005993 Flora of North America, ''Gamochaeta calviceps'' (Fernald) Cabrera, 1961. ]</ref>

''Gamochaeta calviceps'' is similar to ''[[Gamochaeta falcata|G. falcata]],'' and many ''G. calviceps'' specimens from the United States have long been misidentified as ''[[Gamochaeta falcata|G. falcata]].''<ref name=gln/>
